newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity lower on cash, unit returns.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity lower on cash, unit returns.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mostly lower at midday Tuesday, backing off morning strength under pressure from lower physical prices and the return of several Western generation units, sources said.
Spot power prices in the West were said to be off more than $1.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Tuesday as traders looked for power generation to rise as several generation units resumed production.
"Real-time prices are off, and several units are in the restart phase," said a Houston-based futures trader.
As of 1230 EDT, May Palo Verde (PV) was down five cents at $15.90 per MWh, while June was off five cents at $16.80 from exchanges in a range of $16.75-16.95
September PV was off 15 cents at $22.50 per MWh.
May California Oregon Border (COB) was down 14 cents at $12.75 from exchanges in a range of $12.60-13.00, while June was down three cents at $12.35 from trade in a range of $12.20-12.45 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1200 EDT an estimated 98 COB and 145 PV contracts traded.

Over the short term, several generation units were returning to service in the West, including the 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 2, which was at full power Tuesday following a brief weekend outage.

Also, Pacific Gas & Electric Co's 1,212 MW Helms pumped storage hydroelectric plant near Fresno, Calif., was said to be operating at its designed capacity after being shut in early February for fire damage.
The 750 MW Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Ariz., was said to have returned to full power Monday after being shut last month for unplanned maintenance.
Some production capacity remained off line, however, including the 1,080 MW San Onofre unit 2 in southern California and the 1,158 MW WNP-2 plant in Washington.
But sources said a recent slowdown in spring runoff conditions in the Northwest was likely to mean increased reserves of water for hydroelectric generation later in the year.

Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest were forecast to continue to average near to slightly above normal, while readings in the Southwest were called to run four to 10 degrees Fahrenheit above normal through the early part of the weekend.
COB open interest for April 14 fell 19 to 2,458, while PV open interest rose 67 to 4,668, NYMEX said.
